settings.heading: Look good, feel good.
settings.image_alt: Man stepping out of a black Rolls-Royce at night

settings.title: Easy on
settings.body: Front on the lobe, magnet behind it. It pulls itself into place. Two seconds, one hand, no mirror, no help from anyone.

settings.title: Stays on
settings.body: It will not shake loose, sweat off, or get dragged out by a jersey coming over your head. It holds through contact and sits flat enough for headgear to go over it.

settings.title: Off when you say so
settings.body: Pinch and pull. Coming off takes a deliberate move with two fingers, which is exactly what you want when a ref asks you to take it out before tip-off.

settings.image_alt: Man wearing a stud, shot in low light
settings.heading: To be the best you need to feel like it.
settings.intro: Confidence is not a small thing. It is also useless if you spend the whole game checking your ear.

settings.image_alt: Profile of a man wearing a stud
settings.name: Standard
settings.text: The one most guys land on. Visible from across the court, not from space.

settings.image_alt: Man in sunglasses wearing a mid-size stud
settings.name: Loud
settings.text: You want people to notice. They will.

settings.heading: Find your fit in 10 seconds.
settings.intro: Every kit ships with both sizes. Put each one on, look in the mirror, keep the one that looks like it was made for your face. No measuring, no guessing, no exchange.

settings.title: Clothes make the man.
settings.body:
"Clothes make the man. Naked people have little or no influence on society."

Mark Twain, More Maxims of Mark

Nobody is asking you to be loud. They are noticing either way, so the only question is what they notice.

settings.title: Dressing well is a form of good manners.
settings.body:
"Dressing well is a form of good manners."

Tom Ford

Turning up put together is something you do for the room, not just for the mirror. A stud is the smallest version of that.

settings.title: Know first who you are.
settings.body:
"Know, first, who you are, and then adorn yourself accordingly."

Epictetus, Discourses

Two thousand years old and still the whole argument: decide who you are, then dress the part until it is true.

settings.image_alt: Man wearing a stud in the barber chair
settings.heading: The Only Earring Designed for Success
settings.intro: How you present yourself is not vanity. It is the first thing anyone learns about you, and in time it becomes the thing you believe about yourself.
settings.closer: Put it on in two seconds. Take it off when you decide.
